A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same simultaneous-pretraining study and retain the ten original interventions. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original results from training a 1.5B-parameter model on 210B tokens, including reasoning, memorization, poisoning, training-dynamics, and continual-pretraining dependence experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds model-scaling experiments, canary comparisons, general-capability evaluations, and dependence-testing analyses.

M1.justification: The simultaneous-training framework, ten interventions, knowledge-control Algorithm 1, Gaussian-watermark construction, and CPDT matrix procedure remain unchanged. Additional model sizes and statistical analyses extend their evaluation rather than revise these core procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds supplementary evaluation on NQ, DROP, AGIEval, GSM8K, MMLU Pro, and TQA alongside the retained OLMES benchmarks. The original training-data mix and ten intervention tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds OLMo-2-1B controls to the watermark and contamination plots, directly compares Gaussian watermarks, rare-token canaries, and non-canary membership inference in Figure 4, and introduces the full 4T-token model comparison in Table 4. The original comparator families are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds training evaluations at 179M, 546M, and 2.7B parameters and CPDT evaluations with 7B and 13B checkpoints. New protocols vary intervention intensity and compare 50, 100, and 500 training steps while holding inserted data constant. Appendix G also specifies a single-inclusion canary comparison. These extend the evaluation design substantially; the original 1.5B training protocol remains.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 add a comparative canary case study and model-size analyses. Appendices F.3–F.5 investigate larger-model dependence, intervention-strength sensitivity, and training-duration sensitivity. These substantially expand robustness testing beyond v1's retained alternative-checkpoint analysis.

E5.justification: V1 already reports bootstrap intervals for canary results. V2 additionally develops range-based '2000-Step Confidence Intervals' from 20 checkpoint measurements without intervention, adds significance markings to the main dependence matrix, and explicitly identifies 99% reasoning and 90% contamination intervals. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing additional independent pretraining runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds scaling, canary ROC, general-benchmark, and CPDT sensitivity results. Existing results also change: Figure 2c's watermark curve is revised, and the ALL/GW matrix entry changes from 1.6 in v1 Figure 4b to 6.9 in v2 Figure 6b. Figure 25 fills the previously missing IID row and GW entry in v1 Figure 22. The original mathematical-reasoning table remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 5.1 and the Gaussian-watermark equations are retained. Appendix F.6 adds a range-based interval construction and an independence assumption supporting its claimed formal 95% coverage. This introduces limited mathematical reasoning, although no full proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central feasibility, replication, independence-testing, and minimal-training-impact claims remain. The abstract and contribution list extend validation from one 1.5B model to models up to 2.7B parameters, and the introduction adds release of an OLMo-2/OLMo-3 experimentation package as a contribution.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's explanation that weaker joint CPDT effects reflect harder simultaneous learning. It adds explanations involving stronger baseline reasoning in larger models, intervention-strength versus training-stability tradeoffs, and explicit uncertainty about applicability beyond language and unsupervised learning. The principal applicability restrictions remain.

D1.justification: V1 provides model/data links and upstream training-code references. V2 documents a project-specific Python package, links models at four sizes, adds a reproducibility statement, and consolidates resources in Appendix H. New appendices specify larger-model checkpoints and canary-comparison sample counts. These substantially expand documented reproducibility resources; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: V2 adds limited references supporting practical combined interventions, evaluation noise, scaling, standard membership inference, and OLMo-3, including Heineman et al. and Shokri et al. It removes the Hayes et al. citation. The main research positioning is retained; the data-mixtures discussion moves to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion receive localized rewrites. V2 adds subsections for new analyses, organizes Appendix F into named subsections, moves the data-mixtures paragraph, and adds reproducibility and resource sections. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds eleven figures and a general-capability table, including canary ROC curves, scaling plots, sensitivity panels, and interval illustrations. Existing plots gain controls, revised legends, and significance highlighting. The document also adopts ICLR formatting and substantially rearranges figure placement, beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: V1's central feasibility claim rested mainly on one model size and limited CPDT robustness checks. V2 directly strengthens that evidence through multiple trained model sizes, larger-model dependence tests, and intervention-strength and duration ablations. Added controls and documented code resources further improve interpretability and reproducibility. The new interval coverage claim remains conditional on its independence assumption, but the broader empirical validation substantially improves the paper overall.
